summary.text: Jonathan Nez is the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 2nd Congressional District, a rematch with Republican incumbent Eli Crane, who beat him in 2024. A former Navajo Nation vice president and president, he is running on lowering costs, water and rural infrastructure, and accountability in Washington.

paragraphs.text: Nez was born in Tuba City, Arizona, and raised in Shonto, Arizona.
His campaign website says he grew up "on dirt floors without electricity or running water."
He attended Northland Pioneer College and Northern Arizona University, where he earned a bachelor's degree in political science and a Master of Public Administration.

Nez began his political career as vice president of the Shonto Chapter and was later elected to three terms as a Navajo Nation Council delegate representing the Shonto, Oljato, Tsah Bii' Kin and Navajo Mountain chapters. He also served two terms on the Navajo County Board of Supervisors for District 1.
He left the board after being asked to run with Russell Begaye for the Navajo Nation's top offices; the two were elected on April 21, 2015, and took office on May 12, 2015.
Nez was elected Navajo Nation president in November 2018 and served from 2019 to 2023, including during the COVID-19 pandemic.
In August 2020 he was one of 17 Democrats chosen to share the keynote address at the Democratic National Convention.
He was also one of Arizona's presidential electors in 2020. In November 2022 he lost his bid for a second term to Buu Nygren.
Nez ran for Congress in Arizona's 2nd District in 2024, losing to Crane with 45.5 percent of the vote to Crane's 54.5 percent.
He announced a second run on July 22, 2025, and advanced from the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary.
His campaign website says that as Navajo Nation president he worked with the Trump administration to expand water rights for rural Arizona.
